hook_line: Total solar eclipses only exist because of a cosmic coincidence, and it is slowly ending.
intro: Total solar eclipses only exist because of a cosmic coincidence, and it is slowly ending.
facts: The Sun is about 400 times wider than the Moon, but it is also about 400 times farther away, so the two look almost exactly the same size in our sky.
During totality the Moon's shadow sweeps across the ground at thousands of kilometers per hour, and the longest possible totality lasts only about seven and a half minutes.
The sky darkens enough for planets and bright stars to appear, temperatures drop several degrees, and many animals behave as if night has fallen.
The Moon drifts nearly 4 centimeters farther from Earth every year, so models suggest that in roughly 600 million years it will look too small to cover the Sun.
outro: Catch one while our planet still has them.
